decision: The eight-question pilot token advantage did not replicate on 50 disjoint-from-pilot questions. Frozen pre-fix PASR@6 achieved 36/50 full-answer passes versus baseline 42/50 and used 62.11% more total tokens. Ship three reproduced lookup/coverage correctness repairs, not a claimed aggregate accuracy/token optimization.

protocol.purpose: Broader model-specific replication, not fresh-to-research held-out validation.
protocol.sampling: reasoning none, no seed/temperature, default service tier, sequential tool calls
protocol.history: Unchanged pilot executor, complete append-only history and raw MCP output, no masking.
protocol.budget: No retries/fallback; reserve before sending, reconcile cache categories, stop on unknown usage.
protocol.primary_comparison: PASR@6 versus baseline@6: paired full-answer source accuracy and mean cumulative input+output tokens.
protocol.grading: Frozen source-grounded criteria; blinded coding-assistant review, not keyword/API self-grading or human validation. Keep failures in denominators.
protocol.analysis: Report every profile, paired answer transitions, per-repository results, bootstrap question-paired token ratios and accuracy differences. No production promotion from non-significance or equal point estimates alone.
protocol.reuse_disclosure: All 50 questions were previously used in local-model research. They are disjoint from the eight-question OpenAI pilot, not a newly authored holdout.

measured_implementation: Unchanged query_contract snapshot from accuracy_tokens_20260927; none of the new production fixes were used in these 200 trajectories.

diagnosis.pilot: Literal stopword names disappeared from symbol/path lookup; bounded held/remainder state discarded requested scope and could falsely imply whole-file possession. Some failures were missing retrieval, others premature stopping or incorrect synthesis despite available source.

catalog.interpretation: Initial system/question and non-tool settings are identical; the measured input-token difference is associated with the different tool catalog. Catalogs recur on later requests, but this does not assign every later token to catalog versus observation/history.

broader_run_kind_filter_observation.interpretation: Recorded kind exclusions are diagnostic, not by themselves proof of alias bugs or caused answer failures.

diagnosis.interpretation: At six calls, mean tool calls are similar (3.52 baseline, 3.58 PASR), unlike the small pilot. The larger catalog and repeatedly submitted history are material overhead. Selection payload size alone does not measure end-to-end tokens. This is diagnosis, not a measured compact-catalog counterfactual.

production_changes.change: Preserve standalone literal stopword identifiers and single path components; only blank find_files queries request unranked listing. Preserve prose filtering.
production_changes.proof: Reproduced on actual temporary source workspaces; source regressions and real OpenAI MCP path lookup.

production_changes.change: Preserve canonical requested ranges in held/remainder metadata; distinguish bounded completion from whole-file possession and leave unread ranges retrievable.
production_changes.proof: Actual MCP before/after reproductions, range-state regressions, and three sequential OpenAI-requested selections.

production_changes.change: Canonicalize both requested and discovered symbol kinds. Native Python classes are accepted by kinds=[class] and aliases without changing reported native labels.
production_changes.proof: First real API smoke revealed the kind-filter bug; preserved zero-result observation, added Python/Rust alias regression, then confirmed Where class at where.py:1-2 via API.

repair_verification.additional_bug: Kind aliases normalized only the caller filter, so native Python class definitions were excluded by kinds=[class]. Normalize both sides, retain native kind labels.

advice: Exact definition: where.py:1-2. Read it with select_context(query='Where', files=['where.py:1-2']).

after_fix_api_confirmation.actor_answer: The returned symbol is the class `Where`, located at `where.py:1–2`.

final_tests.ruff: All checks passed for the three changed production modules and their test modules.

source_grading.method: Arm-blind coding-assistant source review, not independent human validation.

pre_inference_tls_clarification.scope: Grading only. All 50 actor questions and source workspaces unchanged. Original datasets untouched.

correction.previous_description: SSL errors recognized as SSLEOFError or containing UNEXPECTED_EOF_WHILE_READING become BrokenResourceError in standard-compatible mode and EndOfStream otherwise; unrelated SSL errors are re-raised.
correction.description: Within the generic SSLError handler, SSLEOFError or UNEXPECTED_EOF_WHILE_READING becomes BrokenResourceError in standard-compatible mode and EndOfStream otherwise; other errors reaching that handler are re-raised. Earlier WantRead/WantWrite and SSLSyscallError handlers take precedence. Their mechanics are optional unless falsely described.

spending.billing_caveat: Calculated from observed provider token usage and published rates, including cache reads/writes; not an invoice or observed account balance. Excludes unmetered coding-assistant source review and local computation.

limitations: Previously used research questions, disjoint from the eight-question OpenAI pilot; not a new research holdout.
One model configuration, one repetition, ten Python repositories; no universal or cross-language claim.
Bootstrap intervals are exploratory resampling of this convenience sample, not proof of population equivalence.
Caching affects recorded dollars; token comparisons include all cumulative input and output independently of cache discounts.
API dollars computed from usage and published rates, not account balance or invoice; source-review assistant compute excluded.
Schema/output byte diagnostics are bytes, not provider-token attribution.
Broad accuracy/token results describe the old snapshot, not the repaired production implementation. Targeted repair smokes establish correctness/compatibility, not aggregate quality gains.
The first post-fix smoke had successful API transport but exposed a semantic lookup defect. It is retained, not relabeled as a passing lookup.

Within blind review, optional details were not rigidly required. In particular, explaining CERT_NONE sufficed without enumerating cleared unused CA fields; codec-detection and optional Unicode behavior remained substantive. Review notes preserve these boundaries.
next_experiment: Measure reduced or on-demand tool catalog exposure against baseline@4/@6 on a separately frozen set, retaining all source-quality failures and complete cumulative token accounting. Do not change ranking or force extra calls simultaneously.
